scope: Theorem 7.6 (A periodic processor with quadratic sample times) of the manuscript “Prefix Instructions and Incompressible Flows” (preprints/Prefix-Instructions-and-Incompressible-Flows-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8cd581420ec9967a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Every machine and finite input give an effective smooth mean-zero general force on the unit torus, periodic of period one from time zero. Force and velocity have all mixed derivatives bounded and vanish near integer times. Their spatial supports lie in one compact subset of the cube chart. The unique classical periodic zero-data solution is globally smooth with uniformly bounded energy. From the fixed label (1/2, 1/2, 1/4), the event 3/4 < X1(t) < 7/8 occurs exactly when the machine halts. Whenever reached, the configuration after k ordinary steps is encoded at time (k + 1)2.
